name: awesome-qt
desc: A curated list of awesome tools, libraries, and resources for the Qt framework.

resources.name: Official Website
resources.desc: The official website for the Qt framework.

resources.name: Qt Documentation
resources.desc: Official Qt documentation. Massive and comprehensive.

resources.name: Qt Newsletters
resources.desc: The best of Qt, straight to your spam filter.

resources.name: Qt Bug Tracker
resources.desc: If you think you've found a bug with Qt or one of its related projects, report it here (or see if someone else already has).

resources.name: Qt Code Review
resources.desc: See how the Qt maintainers ensure their code is well-written.

resources.name: Source Code
resources.desc: Browse the various source trees that comprise the Qt project. Has mirrors at several GitHub organizations:

resources.name: Mailing Lists
resources.desc: Mailing lists for users and developers of Qt alike. Arguably the best place to communicate directly with Qt's maintainers. Sees frequent activity.

resources.name: Qt Forum
resources.desc: If e-mail's not your thing, then you might also consider getting help or sharing knowledge on the forums.

resources.name: Qt Wiki
resources.desc: The premier source for user-contributed Qt knowledge.

resources.name: IRC
resources.desc: For real-time chat with other Qt developers and users. The most popular channels are on Freenode, and include #qt, #qt-quick, #qt-creator, and #qt-chat.

resources.name: QtForum.org
resources.desc: Not to be confused with the official Qt forum.

resources.name: Emulator
resources.desc: Don't forget about Qt's mobile support!

resources.name: Qompoter
resources.desc: Dependency manager for Qt / C++.

resources.name: Felgo
resources.desc: Cross-platform game engine and app framework that relies heavily on QML. Has a lot of tools and resources, and may even deserve its own list.

resources.name: QtitanChart
resources.desc: Chart generation framework. Commercial.

resources.name: QtitanRibbon
resources.desc: For fans of the ribbons that Microsoft uses in their software. Commercial.

resources.name: #inqlude
resources.desc: The most well-known aggregation of Qt-centric libraries out there. A package manager is also available here.

resources.name: QtPods
resources.desc: Another Qt-centric package manager. If you want to see the offerings without using QtPods, the full list is available here, and can be added to by submitting a pull request.

resources.name: Linux-Apps.com
resources.desc: Despite the name, Linux-Apps.com aggregates a wide variety of Qt-based tools and libraries for both end-users and developers.

resources.name: Stephan Binner's Ubuntu PPAs
resources.desc: Ubuntu users who are hesitant to install anything outside of their package managers can obtain any recent version of Qt from these repositories. Instructions for adding them are found within.

resources.name: Planet Qt
resources.desc: Official aggregation of first-party and third-party Qt-related blogs.

resources.name: ICS
resources.desc: Qt-centric software consulting firm with a really neat blog. Specializes in graphics applications.

resources.name: Mastering Qt File Selectors
resources.desc: Sometimes you need different variations of the same asset, but you won't know which ones to load until runtime. This class will decide for you.

resources.name: Using Self-Signed Certificates in Qt Code
resources.desc: Trust nobody.

resources.name: Integrating C++ with QML
resources.desc: Talk to your scripting language. That's what it's there for.

resources.name: What's new in Qt 5: QStandardPaths
resources.desc: This feature's been around for a few years, but it's still useful enough to warrant an entry on this list.

resources.name: What's New in Qt 5.2: QCommandLineParser
resources.desc: Another oldie, but still a goodie.

resources.name: Woboq
resources.desc: Another software consulting firm that also contributes code to Qt. They seem to specialize in Qt's core architecture.

resources.name: Moc myths debunked
resources.desc: The magic that Qt appears to rely in is really just a bunch of code generators. This post will bring you up to speed on the reality of the moc, the most notable one.

resources.name: QMetaType knows your types
resources.desc: C++ isn't known for having good run-time type information, so Qt brings its own.

resources.name: C++11 in Qt5
resources.desc: Stop writing C++ like it's 2003; learn how you can take advantage of recent C++ features in your Qt applications.

resources.name: QStringLiteral explained
resources.desc: String literals are widely used in many applications; wouldn't it be nice if you could make them faster to access?

resources.name: Nicer debug output in Qt using QT_MESSAGE_PATTERN
resources.desc: It's nice to be able to read your application's logs.

resources.name: KDAB
resources.desc: *Another* consulting firm that specializes in Qt.

resources.name: GammaRay: Taking a deep look into your Qt application
resources.desc: Talk about GammaRay and how it can help you dissect your Qt applications. Talk given at QtCon 2016 by Volker Krause.

resources.name: Multithreading with Qt
resources.desc: I want to make my application do more than once thing at once. What could possibly go wrong? Talk given at QtCon 2016 by Giuseppe D'Angelo.

resources.name: Linux perf for Qt developers
resources.desc: How to make your Qt application faster, Linux-style. Talk given at QtCon 2016 by Milian Wolff.

resources.name: Scythe-Studio
resources.desc: Yet another consulting company specialized in Qt

resources.name: Qt Creator Cheat Sheet
resources.desc: Convenient document for improving your familiarity with Qt Creator IDE.

resources.name: Qt Installer Framework tutorial
resources.desc: Series about practical usage of Qt Installer framework with in-depth overview of different features.

resources.name: How to interface Qt with Android Java code
resources.desc: Getting wild and "native" with Android code in your Qt application.

resources.name: How to use NFC in Qt/Qml application?
resources.desc: Have you ever wondered how to use NFC in Qt/Qml application? This blog post will give you a complex overview of the concept of near-field communication technology with examples of its usage in real life.

resources.name: Autodesk Maya
resources.desc: 3D animation and design software that has been used to create visual effects for some of the most popular movies and TV shows of all time.

resources.name: Davinci Resolve
resources.desc: Non-linear video editing freeware with commercial plan used to create some Hollywood movies.

resources.name: Google Earth
resources.desc: *The* virtual globe.

resources.name: LMMS
resources.desc: Digital audio workstation.

resources.name: Malwarebytes
resources.desc: Your Windows desktop's personal bodyguard.

resources.name: MuseScore
resources.desc: Music notation software.

resources.name: Parallels Desktop
resources.desc: Consumer-focused virtualization.

resources.name: Shotcut
resources.desc: Video editor.

resources.name: RUBE
resources.desc: Level design tool for any game that uses the Box2D physics engine.

resources.name: TeamSpeak
resources.desc: When gamers want to voice chat in a game that doesn't support it, they'll use this.

resources.name: Wolfram Mathematica
resources.desc: Programming language, symbolic calculator, and an engineer's best friend.

resources.name: Awesome C/C++
resources.desc: There's no reason you can't use C++ libraries that weren't designed for Qt. Sometimes they might even suit your needs better than what Qt offers.

resources.name: Awesome C
resources.desc: Same goes for C libraries; might wanna brush up on those RAII techniques while you're at it.

resources.name: Awesome CMake
resources.desc: If you're not using qmake for your project, you're likely using CMake instead.

resources.name: Awesome OpenGL
resources.desc: Qt is commonly used for graphics applications, even providing its own wrappers around OpenGL.
